answer: The knoll assignment is published and opal records each panel. Shards are assigned from the thread graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The grading quorum of 3 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an hostile operator cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 4958 identities would post 950 proofs and burn roughly 37 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
